subject: RFI: TAM coverage, incident communication, and support hours — Crestline Financial
messages:
From: James Park <james.park@crestline-fin.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Crestline Procurement <procure@crestline-fin.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@crestline-fin.com>
Date: 2028-08-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RFI — TAM coverage, escalation matrix, and incident comms (spreadsheet attached)

Hannah,

Thanks for the quick intro call last week. We've consolidated the support/TAM questions into the attached spreadsheet (crestline_rfi_tam_questions.xlsx) — vendor responses will feed directly into our scoring matrix. Can you please provide answers for the following sections by EOD Friday?

- TAM coverage model (dedicated vs shared) and hours (local support, 24/7, regional overlap)
- Escalation routing (who gets paged for Sev1/Sev2, SLA ack/mitigation timeframes)
- Communication cadence for incidents (customer-facing updates, cadence for root cause updates)
- Attachments/evidence you can share (escalation matrix, on-call roster, sample incident comms)

Also note any constraints for private deployments (VPC/on-prem) related to on-call handoffs and runbooks.

Appreciate it — happy to set a short follow-up review once we have your responses.

Best,
James Park
Director, Infrastructure Procurement
Crestline Financial

Attachment: crestline_rfi_tam_questions.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: James Park <james.park@crestline-fin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-09T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI — TAM coverage, escalation matrix, and incident comms (answers + draft matrix)

James — thanks for sending this over and for the clear template. We took the spreadsheet and answered each line; see inline in the attached and a short summary below. Also attaching a draft escalation matrix (proposed_escalation_matrix_v2.pdf) for your review.

Summary (high level):
- TAM coverage model: Shared TAMs by default for accounts of this size; option to convert to dedicated TAM for committed Dedicated capacity contracts. Shared TAMs are assigned per region with overlap windows.
- Support hours: Business-hours SL (Mon–Fri 08:00–18:00 local) included. 24/7 coverage for Sev1 incidents via on-call rotation (global overlap provides night coverage).
- Escalation & SLA targets (proposed):
  - Sev1 (system-down / service unavailable): 1 hour ack, 4 hour initial mitigation plan, continuous updates every 2 hours until mitigation
  - Sev2 (major degradation): 2 hour ack, 8 hour mitigation plan, updates at least twice daily
  - Sev3/4 (minor/maintenance): next-business-day response
- Incident communications: Customer-facing updates from the TAM/CS lead at the cadence above; formal RCA within 5 business days for Sev1, 10 business days for Sev2 (can align to your procurement timeline).
- Evidence package: We can provide SOC 2 summary, incident notification examples, and the escalation matrix draft attached. Full audit logs and longer retention are available on Private deployments; please flag if you need a compliance addendum.

Next steps / asks for Crestline:
- Confirm whether you require a dedicated TAM (and if so, whether that must be strictly single-tenant)
- Preferred timezone for weekly incident sync (we typically propose UTC or EST for NA customers)
- If you want PagerDuty/OPSGenie integration, tell us your existing provider and org key so we can map escalation endpoints

We'll be happy to join a 30-min Q&A once you review.

Attachments: proposed_escalation_matrix_v2.pdf (application/pdf); crestline_rfi_tam_questions_filled.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer — Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Hannah — quick clarification after skimming the matrix: is the 24/7 on-call coverage you note a dedicated, customer-only on-call (single-tenant) or a shared rotation where Redwood engineers handle Sev1 for multiple customers? Also, for Sev2 you list an 8-hour mitigation plan — is that a firm SLA or a target (we need to understand what is contractual versus operational best-effort).

If possible, can you mark the cells in the spreadsheet as "Contractual (SLA)" vs "Operational target" and resend? We'll use that in our scoring.

Thanks,
James
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-11T15:43:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: RFI — TAM coverage, escalation matrix, and incident comms (details requested)

Karthik — forwarding Crestline's clarification and our draft responses. They want explicit labeling of contractual vs operational. Can you confirm the following from an engineering/runtime perspective so we can mark the spreadsheet and finalize:

- For Dedicated customers (we have Dedicated capacity contract): confirm we can guarantee dedicated on-call escalation routing to assigned on-call (single-tenant) and produce SLA language for Sev1 acknowledgements.
- For Shared TAM/on-call model: confirm that on-call rotation is shared across customers and that we can commit to the Ack times as SLAs only when on Dedicated; otherwise treat as operational targets.
- PagerDuty/OpsGenie integrations: can we supply org-level webhook mapping and produce a sample alert payload and recommended alerting thresholds?
- Runbook hooks: can the runtime send structured incident webhooks (event JSON) and do we have a standard retention/privacy posture for traces and KV cache logs (what retention options can we offer on Private vs Hosted)?

Please add any hard constraints or product notes inline in the attached spreadsheet. We need the completed version back to send to Crestline by 8/12 EOD.

Marissa
Head of Customer Success Operations
Redwood Inference
